SRI.N.S.NAJEEB, STANDING COUNSEL  K.S.SANTHI  THIS MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS APPEAL HAVING BEEN FINALLY HEARD ON 07.02.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 MACA. No.2196/2015  3  2025:KER:16676  JUDGMENT Dated this the 7th day of February, 2025
The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.) No.1683/2006 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Thiruvananthapuram is the appellant herein.

(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).
2.

The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 166 and 140 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988,
claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 27.4.2006.

According to the petitioner, on 27.4.2006 at about 7 a.m. while he was riding pillion on a motor cycle bearing registration No.KL-01-AD-4211, ridden by the 1 st respondent in a rash and negligent manner, it dashed against another motor cycle bearing registration No.KL-01-AK-4466,
which came in opposite direction.
As a result of the accident, the petitioner sustained serious injuries.

2 3.

sentences.text: The 1st respondent is the rider and 2nd respondent is the insurer of the motor cycle KL-01-AD-4211.
3rd and 4th respondents are the owner and insurer of the motor cycle bearing registration No.KL-01-AK-4466.
According to the petitioner, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the 2025:KER:16676 1st respondent, the driver of the offending vehicle.

The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P. is Rs.3,50,000/-.
4.
The 2nd respondent/insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

5. The evidence in the case consists of the documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A13.
6.

After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal found negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, awarded a total compensation of Rs.1,41,700/- and directed the insurer/2nd respondent to pay the same.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?

9. Heard Sri. R. Nikhil, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner/appellant, and Sri. N.S.
Najeeb, the learned Standing Counsel for the 2nd respondent.
The Point: In this case the accident as well as valid policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.
One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner is regarding the income of the petitioner as fixed by the Tribunal.
According to him, the petitioner was working as carpenter earning Rs.4,000/- per month, but the Tribunal fixed his monthly income at Rs3,500/-.
The learned counsel for the insurer would argue that the income fixed by the tribunal is reasonable.

11. As per the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the notional income of a coolie, in the year 2006 will come to Rs.5,500/- Since the petitioner could not prove his job or income as claimed in the OP, in the light of a dictum laid down in the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ramachandrappa (supra), his notional income is liable to be fixed as that of a coolie, at Rs.5500/-.
12.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the accident the petitioner sustained the following injuries:
"Fracture of neck of femur and fracture shaft of (L) femur and multiple facial bones."

sentences.text:
As per Ext. A13 disability certificate issued by Additional Professor of Orthopaedics, Medical College Hospital, Thiruvananthapuram 2025:KER:16676 shows that the petitioner suffered 20%
permanent physical disability.

The Doctor has noticed the features of the petitioner at the time of examination on 27.5.2014 as follows:
"Long scars on left thigh over right iliac crest.
Implants in situ in left thigh and hip.
Partial ankylosis of left knee with flexion limited to 95 degrees.
Crepitus and pain present in left knee.
External rotation deformity of 10 degree of left lower limb.
Internal rotation of left hip not present.
Shortening of lcm of left lower limb.
Wasting of l cm of left thigh muscles.
Patient walks with limp.
Not able to squat.
Difficulty in climbing stairs and getting downstairs, Difficulty in carrying weight.
Difficulty in doing Carpenter work.
The fracture of lower end of left radius has united with diner fork deformity and volar subluxation of head of ulna.
Palmar flexion of left wrist limited to 10 degrees.
Weakness of grip strength of left hand with Grade IV+ power."
14. The Tribunal, however, scaled down the percentage of disability of the petitioner to 10%, without assigning valid and cogent reasons.

The law is settled that, if the Tribunal is not satisfied with the disability certificate produced by the petitioner, the remedy is to refer him to a medical board or 2025:KER:16676 higher Authority.(See Manikantan G. v. Janardhanan Nair and Others, 2021 (5)KHC 305).

entities.text: Manikantan G. v. Janardhanan Nair and Others, 2021 (5)KHC 305)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Having not done so, the Tribunal was not justified in scaling down the percentage of disability from what is shown in the disability certificate.
I do find any grounds to disbelieve the said disability and as such the permanent physical disability of the petitioner is fixed as 20%.
15. On the date of accident, the petitioner was aged 34 years.

Therefore, 40% of the monthly income is to be added towards future prospects, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co. Ltd. v.
Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680] and the multiplier to be applied is 16, as held in Sarla Verma v.
Delhi Transport Corporation [(2009) 6 SCC 121].

sentences.text:
In the above circumstances, the loss of disability will come to Rs.2,95,680/-
16.
Towards loss of earning, the tribunal has awarded Rs.21,000/- being the income for 6 months @Rs.3500/-.

Since the notional income of the petitioner is re-fixed at Rs.5,500/-, towards loss of earning he is entitled to get a sum of Rs. 33,000/- (5,500 x 6months)
17.
Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has awarded Rs.15000/-.
Towards 'loss of amenities of life' Rs.10,000/- was awarded and towards 'extra nourishment' Rs.2,000/- was awarded.
According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, the compensation awarded on those heads are on 2025:KER:16676 the lower side.

Babu vs Sabu on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33070975/
4 18.
The petitioner sustained very serious injuries including 3 fractures in the accident and was treated as inpatient for 21 days.

Because of the injuries sustained, the percentage of disability suffered and the length of treatment undergone by the petitioner, I hold that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on the heads 'pain and sufferings', 'loss of amenities of life' and 'extra nourishment' are on the lower side and hence they are enhanced to Rs.30,000/- , Rs.20,000/- and Rs.5,000/- respectively.
19. No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.

20. Therefore, the petitioners/appellants are entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.4,10,180/-,
as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference:
Sl.
 No. Head of Claim Amount awarded by Amount Awarded in  Tribunal (in Rs.) Appeal (in Rs.)
 1 Loss of earning 21,000/- 33,000/-
 2 Transportation 2,000/- 2,000/-
 3 Damage to clothing 500/- 5,00/-
 4

Medical expenses 21,000/- 21,000/-
 5 Bystander expenses 3,000/- 3,000/-
 2025:KER:16676  6

Extra nourishment 2,000/- 5,000/-
 7 Pain and suffering 15,000/- 30,000/-
 8 Compensation for disability 67,200/- 2,95,680/-
 9 Loss of amenities in life 10,000/- 20,000/-

Enhanced Rs.2,68,480/-
21. In the result, this Appeal is allowed in part, and Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit a total sum of Rs.4,10,180/- (Rupees four lakh ten thousand one hundred and eighty Only), less the amount already deposited, if any, along with interest at the rate ordered by the Tribunal, from the date of the petition till deposit/realisation, with proportionate costs, within a period of two months from today.
(enhanced compensation will carry interest @8%).

5

excluding court fee payable, if any, without delay, as per rules.

C. PRATHEEP KUMAR, JUDGE sou.
